candidates.rationale: The implementation delegates to variant-specific address semantics, but current vstd has no public model of IpAddr, Ipv4Addr, or Ipv6Addr contents from which loopback membership can be specified.
risks: Any deterministic postcondition would require inventing an IP-address view or relying on unmodeled methods.

candidates.rationale: Multicast membership depends on the contained IPv4 or IPv6 address, for which current vstd provides no public address-content abstraction.
risks: Encoding multicast ranges requires a missing IP-address view.

candidates.rationale: The source delegates to Ipv4Addr and Ipv6Addr semantics, but no existing vstd view exposes whether the contained address is all zeroes.
risks: A useful result relation requires a new model of IP address components.

candidates.rationale: Canonicalization preserves IPv4 values and converts IPv4-mapped IPv6 values, but current vstd cannot express either condition because it lacks modeled IP-address contents.
risks: Specifying mapped-address detection or the converted result requires a new IP-address abstraction.

candidates.rationale: The source defines the result through big-endian octets, but current vstd has no view of Ipv4Addr octets or modeled inverse operation with which to relate the result to bits.
risks: A postcondition requires an Ipv4Addr octet view or corresponding modeled accessor.

candidates.rationale: Although construction is deterministic, current vstd has no public view exposing an Ipv4Addr's four octets, so no useful observable result relation can be written.
risks: Constructor semantics require a new Ipv4Addr octet abstraction.
